title: Dance programs: waltz, polka, mazurka, schottische and quadrille sets
summary: He doesn't recall specific pieces but describes the order of dances at balls, including the Virginia reel.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Do you remember some of the pieces you played? Well, I remember which numbers.
No, I never did. I never did pay much attention to the, to the pieces that was played.
Were they marches or waltzes or what kind of pieces? Well, yeah, you know. All the ones.
You take in, in the time that I used to go to dances, I used to play at dances.
Well, that's what he wants to know. What pieces you played?

What kind? We used to play waltz first, then polka, then a mazooka, and then a shardish, and then a square dance. We had to be alliances. Yes. Then you'd come back, waltz, polka, mazooka, shardish, and a variety. That's two square dances. You understand? Yes. And then when the next square dance time would come, it'd be a little lances again, you see, and then the next time, variety. That was good times then.
And sometimes, sometimes the middle of the night, when you come, because that time the ball just did all night. That play a Virginia reel. That come in. That was good.
